messages:
tim: hey team :wave: I'm Tim (new infra hire). First day — trying to run the repo's CI from my fork and hitting a 403 when pulling the runner image. Which GitHub App/permission did I miss?

alex: welcome Tim! quick answer: you probably need the GitHub App installed at the org level with packages read access. also make sure you accepted the app install invite.

tim: here is the exact error from buildkite agent:
```
error: GET https://ghcr.io/v2/redwood/ci-runner/manifests/latest 403
{"message":"access denied","documentation_url":"https://docs.github.com/packages"}
```

jamie: and for Buildkite itself you'll need membership in the ci-buildkite Okta group (that gives the agent token and pipeline perms). @priya can add you.

priya: adding Tim to ci-buildkite group now, give me a minute and then try to restart the job. also check you accepted the onboarding checklist item "Install GitHub App" under Getting Started.

infra-bot: Access request created: CI-4521 assigned to #infra-oncall. Status: pending.

tim: re-ran after ~6m, still 403 and buildkite shows "failed to pull image: denied". build link: https://buildkite.com/redwood/infra-pipeline/builds/123

alex: hmm — did you add any personal PATs? our pipeline uses the org GitHub App token (not PAT) for GHCR. If the app wasn't installed on the fork/repo it will fail.

jamie: I checked org settings — the app install was missing for that repo because forks don't inherit org installs. Installed the app on the repo now.

priya: also confirmed Tim is in ci-buildkite group.

jamie: Tim, can you restart the Buildkite job (there's a little "Restart build" button on the build page)?

tim: restarting now...

tim: ✅ build succeeded! thanks everyone :tada: — feel free to DM if I should run any post-onboarding checks.

alex: nice one. welcome aboard! :thumbsup:
